answer: The lantern counter is kept in jetty and shale makes public each reset. An hostile operator as a result has to keep every alias continuously active for 49 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 49 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 394 aliases cost 57 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
